observations: Onboarding progress is rendered as a segmented 3-part progress bar at the top (`.onboarding-progress` with three `.step-dot` divs, first segment filled indigo on the welcome step), supported by the named step checklist 'Set up your profile' / 'Create your first project' / 'You're all set' with per-step hint text and check-circle icons.

The empty state (renderDashboard, projects.length === 0) is a folder-with-plus SVG in `.empty-icon`, the heading 'No projects yet', one supporting sentence, and a 'New project' primary button — graphical icon with text support.

Transient states are also graphical: the load screen shows a `.spinner` plus 'Loading your workspace…', and the create button swaps to an inline 18px spinner plus 'Creating…' while `creatingProject` is true.

Metrics count 5 graphical indicators on the idle view (svg: 4, badges: 1); progress/meter/role=progressbar are 0 because the step bar is styled divs rather than a semantic progress element, but it is visually a progress indicator.

The page is lean: desktop viewportWords = pageWords = 48, helperWords = 16, and the only long leaf is the 16-word subtitle 'Set up your workspace in under a minute. We'll get you organized and ready to go.'
Button labels are terse: labels count 2, meanWords 2, maxWords 2, longLabels empty; across the source the longest labels are 'Create project' and 'New project' (2 words).

A few sentences are pep or restate the UI: the second half of the welcome subtitle adds nothing, and the empty-state paragraph restates the 'No projects yet' heading and the 'New project' button beside it.

Step subtitles ('Confirm your details so your team knows who you are.', 'Pick a template to get started quickly, or create a blank project.') are single lines, not paragraphs — the UI does not narrate itself.

Copy promises behavior that does not happen: the success toast 'Project "<name>" created!' fires after createProject(), but the code only calls api.updateSettings({ hasCompletedOnboarding: true }) and never adds a project, so the confirmed dashboard shows 'No projects yet' immediately after claiming the project was created (also flagged by the async rater under item 10).

'Pick a template or start blank' (checklist hint) and 'or create a blank project' (step-2 subtitle) promise a blank option, but the template grid offers only Marketing/Engineering/Design/Personal with no blank card or control; starting blank is only implicitly possible by ignoring the grid.
'We'll get you organized and ready to go.' is marketing pep in a tool UI that adds no information beyond the preceding sentence.
Terminology and behavior are otherwise consistent (project/template/workspace used uniformly; 'Skip setup' does skip; 'Back' does go back), which keeps this at 3 issues, in the 2-to-4 band.

The structure is genuinely shaped by the brief: a 3-step first-run wizard (welcome → profile → first project) ending in a dashboard whose zero-project branch is a designed empty state with 'No projects yet' and a 'New project' CTA — exactly the no-projects new user.

Personalization is real, not decorative: 'Welcome to Planwise, Alex' uses user.name from api.getUser(), the profile step pre-fills name/email from the API, and buildTimezoneOptions() preselects the visitor's timezone via Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone.

The template gallery (📣 Marketing 'Campaign tracking and content calendar', ⚙️ Engineering 'Sprint planning and bug tracking', 🎨 Design, 📝 Personal) with name autofill ('Marketing Project') is a project-management-specific onboarding choice, plus an explicit 'Skip setup' escape hatch.

The visual layer is stock SaaS: Inter from Google Fonts, indigo #4f6ef7-family accent, centered white card wizard, bottom-right toast stack — competent but interchangeable styling, which holds the score at 4 rather than 5.
From the idle desktop screenshot alone: the page is clearly the first-run setup of a project tool ('Welcome to Planwise, Alex' + 'Set up your workspace in under a minute'), matching the brief.
The primary action is unambiguous: 'Get started' is the only solid indigo button, bottom-right of the card, with 'Skip setup' correctly demoted to a ghost button on the left.

What needs attention reads correctly as the three-step checklist ('Set up your profile', 'Create your first project', 'You're all set') and the top progress bar with the first of three segments filled — the checklist item 'Create your first project' directly names the brief's goal.
All three answers checked out against the brief and source; nothing on the screen competes with the wizard (48 visible words total).
